groups.name: RL algorithms & sample-efficient learning
groups.description: Methodological improvements to reinforcement-learning training: off-policy estimators, replay buffers, demonstration weighting, augmentation, and learning-progress curricula.

groups.name: Safe RL with boundary, recovery, & geofence constraints
groups.description: Mechanisms that bound RL behavior to safe regions via composite policies, geofences, hard limits, support constraints, or reachability-based recovery.

groups.name: Multi-agent coordination, Stackelberg games, & cooperation
groups.description: Theoretical and empirical work on cooperation among multiple agents, including Stackelberg decompositions, partner-similarity manifolds, delegation, and coordinated command.

groups.name: Mechanistic interpretability & circuit analysis
groups.description: Analyses of how facts, circuits, and behaviors are localized in transformer layers and CNN filters, including state-machine embeddings and logit-lens diagnostics.

groups.name: Formal verification & certified robustness
groups.description: Formal-methods approaches yielding provable bounds: certified radii, flow-pipe reachability, model checking, and worst-case loss bounds.

groups.name: OOD detection & calibrated uncertainty
groups.description: Methods for detecting distribution shift and producing calibrated uncertainty estimates, including Bayesian monitors, alternative scores, and condition-number triggers.

groups.name: AI governance, licensing, & regulatory enforcement
groups.description: Policy and institutional mechanisms governing AI release, deployment, and oversight: licenses, regulator hiring, antitrust, export controls, evaluations partnerships, and educational/race-de-escalation initiatives.

groups.name: Biosecurity, pathogen screening, & pandemic surveillance
groups.description: Interventions and evidence on biological risk reduction: wastewater monitoring, Far-UVC, DNA synthesis screening, biosafety officers, CRISPR governance, and historical quarantine.

groups.name: Compute governance & semiconductor industrial policy
groups.description: Strategic-resource arguments around GPU supply, SME market dominance, and consortium-style industrial policy for chips.

groups.name: AI safety field-building, outreach, & curricula
groups.description: Designs and evidence for growing AI safety capacity: fellowships, curricula, video outreach, dictionaries, Q&A pipelines, and prioritization research programs.

groups.name: LLM prompting, structured output, & citation grounding
groups.description: Techniques to constrain and ground LLM outputs: JSON mode, delimiter prompts, inline evidence syntax, citation training, self-correction loops, and verification warnings.

groups.name: Diffusion & generative model sampling
groups.description: Sampler-design and conditioning improvements for diffusion / generative models, including Heun samplers, FID monitoring, and CLIP prior networks.

groups.name: CNN architectures, receptive fields, & vision benchmarks
groups.description: Convolutional vision research: receptive-field analysis, padding, capsule networks, change-captioning datasets, frequency augmentation, and accuracy benchmarks.

groups.name: Privacy, data protection, & GDPR compliance
groups.description: Data-handling concerns and remedies including GDPR violations, vendor-managed retrieval, knowledge-graph leakage, and Privacy-by-Design principles.

groups.name: Efficient compute: neuromorphic, sparse, & memory-aware inference
groups.description: Hardware- and systems-level mechanisms for efficient training/inference: neuromorphic AER routing, LSH sparse multiplications, FlashAttention, model checking of CPUs, and parameter-equivalent throughput gains.

groups.name: Autonomous drones, robotics, & ROS security
groups.description: Operational and security interventions for autonomous physical systems: drone combat units, ROS TLS/IPSec defaults, geofences, and reset-cost issues in robotic RL.

groups.name: Probabilistic programming, Bayesian, & variational methods
groups.description: Foundational probabilistic-modeling work: Involutive MCMC, FEP, KL-regularized RL as Bayesian update, particle filters, partition-function estimation, and WebPPL inference.

groups.name: Forecasting, aggregation, & AI timeline estimation
groups.description: Methods and findings on probabilistic forecasting and HLMI/timeline elicitation, including question-framing biases, scoring rules, and extremizing aggregation.

groups.name: Catastrophic, TAI, & existential risk theory
groups.description: Theoretical and empirical reasoning about catastrophic AI scenarios and broader x-risk, including diffusion dynamics, instrumental convergence, anthropic bounds, and defense in depth.

groups.name: Global health, philanthropy, & EA interventions
groups.description: Interventions oriented to global health and effective-altruist resource allocation: opioid access, malaria nets, and funding-base volatility.

groups.name: Cybersecurity, AI incident response, & insider threats
groups.description: Operational defenses and threat models for AI systems and adjacent infrastructure: incident playbooks, manual utility fallbacks, fingerprinting, insider-threat programs, and emergency disconnects.

groups.name: Human modeling, motivation, & behavioral nudges
groups.description: Models and interventions treating humans as bounded-rational agents: resource-rational heuristics, near-optimal soft-Q humans, commitment devices, autonomy-supportive language, and habituation.

groups.name: Meta-learning, few-shot, & benchmark datasets
groups.description: Evaluation infrastructure and methods for generalization: Meta-Dataset, QMNIST50, generative grid grammars, StreetView storefront shifts, and CUAD-style annotated corpora.

groups.name: Healthcare AI deployment & clinical workflows
groups.description: Translating AI systems into clinical and consumer health settings with explanation, oversight, and access: explainable triage, wearables, and small-dataset prototypes.

parsed.notes: Inputs span a broad AI-safety/ML stack. Some boundary nodes (e.g., 21 GDPR vs. governance, 92 export controls vs. compute policy) plausibly fit multiple groups; placed in the more specific cluster. ~5–8% of nodes (e.g., 7, 15, 19, 26, 87, 94, 153) are heterogeneous singletons left as residual rather than forced into thin groups.
